transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yes, thank you. I'm Janet. Well, I guess... I'm here because of my eating, which feels a little embarrassing to admit out loud to a professional, but it's really gotten to a point where I don't know what else to do. Since I'm not working right now, I'm just at the house all day, and I guess I spend a lot of time near the kitchen. 

And it's not just that I'm snacking or having an extra cookie here and there, because everybody does that, you know? What really scares me—and I mean it genuinely frightens me—is that once I start eating, especially when I’m completely alone in the kitchen, it's like a switch flips. It feels like I’ve just... stepped aside. Like I'm watching myself do it and I absolutely cannot make myself stop. The whole time it's happening, I’m literally telling myself in my head, over and over, ‘Janet, put it away, just close the pantry door, you don't even want this,’ but it doesn't matter. My hands just keep going, opening packages and getting more food. It’s like I have absolutely no say in the matter once it starts, and I'm just so tired of feeling like I'm not the one in charge of my own body.
Janet, when these episodes happen, do you ever try to compensate for the eating by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot afterward?

Oh, no. No, I don't do anything like that. I know some people do, you know, you read about people making themselves sick in the bathroom, but I have never been able to make myself throw up. Even when I actually have a stomach bug, I will fight it until the bitter end because I just completely despise the feeling of being sick like that, so I could never do it on purpose. And laxatives... no, absolutely not. I actually had a terrible experience with those years ago just for normal stomach issues, and I swore I'd never touch them again. 

As for fasting... well, it's funny you ask that, because in my head, right after an episode happens, I always *plan* to fast. I’ll be sitting there on the sofa, just surrounded by empty wrappers and feeling so completely stuffed and miserable, and I'll promise myself, 'Janet, you are not taking a single bite of food tomorrow, you're just going to drink water and fix this.' But... I never actually do it. The next morning rolls around, and I might skip breakfast because I'm still so full from the night before, but by lunchtime I'm right back in the kitchen eating again, so I really can't say I actually fast. 

And exercise? Goodness, no. I haven't had a gym membership in years, well before I stopped working. When I finish eating like that, I feel so heavy and sluggish and just... ashamed, really. The very last thing I could possibly do is put on sneakers and go for a run or get on a treadmill. I basically just sit there in the quiet and let myself feel awful about what I just did. I just let all that food sit there in my stomach. So, no, I don't do any of those things to try and undo it, even though I probably wish I could undo it.
How often do these episodes happen, and do they cause you a lot of distress?

Well, gosh, if I really think about it... I actually keep a little calendar in the kitchen, just a cheap one I picked up at the dollar store, mostly to keep track of my food bank weeks and when the mail carrier comes, things like that. And looking back at it, because sometimes I'll make a little checkmark or a scribble on the days I feel particularly bad about what I've eaten... it's been happening most weeks. I'd say often once, maybe twice a week. And it's been going on like this for many months now. It didn't just start yesterday, you know? It's been a long, slow slide into this routine. 

And as for distress... oh, absolutely. It's just awful. Like I was saying before, the shame of it is just overwhelming. I sit there and I look at the empty boxes and the wrappers, and I just think, 'How did I let this happen again?' It's a very lonely feeling, too, because I'm by myself, and I can't exactly call up a friend and say, 'Hey, I just ate an entire family-sized bag of chips and half a loaf of bread in twenty minutes.' They wouldn't understand. They'd just say, 'Well, why didn't you stop?' And that's the whole point, isn't it? I can't stop. So yes, it causes me an immense amount of distress. It's really taking a toll on my mental state, just feeling so out of control all the time. It's exhausting, honestly. Just completely exhausting to fight with yourself and lose, week after week.
